title: Synodical letter: Scripture says ‘adore’ absolutely, but ‘serve/cult’ with ‘alone’—so latria is referred to God only
source_text: IX. His consona sunt quae leguntur Actione septima in epistola Synodica ad Augustos, quam supra citavimus. Divina Scriptura dicens, Deum tuum adorabis, & illi soli cultum exhibebis: adorabis absolute ponit, neque adjicit, soli, ut significetur vox diversae notionis & aequivoca. Cultum vero exhibebis sive servire soli dixit: quam ob causam latriam uni Deo tribuimus, adque illum referimus.
pass_a_gloss: Consonant with these are the things which are read in the seventh Action in the Synodical epistle to the Augusti, which we cited above. Divine Scripture saying, You shall adore your God, and to him alone you shall exhibit cult: ‘you shall adore’ it puts absolutely, nor does it add ‘alone,’ that it may be signified that the word is of diverse notion and equivocal. But ‘you shall exhibit cult’ or ‘serve’ it said with ‘alone’: for which cause we attribute latria to the one God, and refer it to him.
pass_b_english: The Synod’s letter to the emperors: Scripture’s ‘adore’ stands without ‘alone,’ so the word is equivocal.
‘Serve/cult’ carries ‘alone’—hence latria is ascribed and referred to God only (Deuteronomy 6:13; Matthew 4:10).

lemmas.gloss: a word of diverse sense and equivocal

choices.why: Exegetical warrant for non-latria ‘adoration’ of images.
